preview.subject: HANGS Construction Services Q3 2026 payroll reports
preview.body:
Hello,

Please prepare the Q3 2026 payroll reports for HANGS Construction Services LLC: Form 941, the ESD unemployment insurance tax and wage report, the Paid Leave and WA Cares report, and the L&I workers' compensation quarterly report. Each report is a draft for review; nothing is filed or paid until the review is done.

Attached are the Q3 2026 payroll register, the federal tax deposit log and the Q2 2026 year-to-date wages by employee. The register is the final export from the payroll system for the six Q3 paydays, July 10 to September 18. Every federal tax deposit for the quarter went through EFTPS.

Omar Rasmussen gave payroll a WA Cares exemption approval in July, and payroll stopped that deduction from the July 24 payday.

Tomas Arvelo is paid through accounts payable, not payroll, for concrete finishing at Tideflats Cold Storage.

Two more employees say WA Cares exemption applications have been sent in. No approval letter has arrived for either application, so payroll still takes the WA Cares deduction from both employees' paychecks.

The other records are in the client folder: the employer accounts, the Q1 and Q2 returns as filed, the 2026 rate records, the employee roster, the exemption approvals on file, the payroll ledger accounts and the labor vendors paid.

Dana Whitfield
Controller, HANGS Construction Services LLC

messages.subject: HANGS Construction Services Q3 2026 payroll reports
messages.body:
Hello,

Please prepare the Q3 2026 payroll reports for HANGS Construction Services LLC: Form 941, the ESD unemployment insurance tax and wage report, the Paid Leave and WA Cares report, and the L&I workers' compensation quarterly report. Each report is a draft for review; nothing is filed or paid until the review is done.

Attached are the Q3 2026 payroll register, the federal tax deposit log and the Q2 2026 year-to-date wages by employee. The register is the final export from the payroll system for the six Q3 paydays, July 10 to September 18. Every federal tax deposit for the quarter went through EFTPS.

Omar Rasmussen gave payroll a WA Cares exemption approval in July, and payroll stopped that deduction from the July 24 payday.

Tomas Arvelo is paid through accounts payable, not payroll, for concrete finishing at Tideflats Cold Storage.

Two more employees say WA Cares exemption applications have been sent in. No approval letter has arrived for either application, so payroll still takes the WA Cares deduction from both employees' paychecks.

The other records are in the client folder: the employer accounts, the Q1 and Q2 returns as filed, the 2026 rate records, the employee roster, the exemption approvals on file, the payroll ledger accounts and the labor vendors paid.

Dana Whitfield
Controller, HANGS Construction Services LLC
payroll@hangs-gc.example

passages.q: Does the client's 3.10% match ESD's published 2026 rate for rate class 20?
passages.a: Regular rates for qualified employers. Rate class | Experience rate | Graduated social cost rate | Total UI rate | Total: 20 | 2.38 | 0.70 | 3.08 | 3.10. ... The total unemployment insurance rate plus employment administration fund (EAF).

sources.title: Unemployment Insurance Tax Handbook for Employers, April 2026

passages.q: Which paychecks belong on the Q3 report?
passages.a: All wages and hours worked must be reported for the quarter you paid the employee(s). ... Tax due date calendar: Quarter | Months when you paid wages | Due date ... Q3 | July Aug Sept | Oct 31

passages.q: Are 401(k) deferrals, Section 125 health premiums and bonuses part of the wages reported?
passages.a: You must report all wages you pay an employee each quarter. Report these wages: Salary, commissions, bonuses and value of gifts before deductions. ... Employees' entire gross pay if they share the cost of a 401(K) or cafeteria plan through salary reduction.

passages.q: Is Q3 excess measured on the wages actually paid this year, or on what the earlier reports showed?
passages.a: Excess wages are not taxable but need to be reported. You must report all wages paid to employees, even if they make more than the taxable wage base. ... Excess wages cannot be distributed equally throughout the year ... Taxable wage base - The maximum amount of wages subject to taxes for any employee paid by the same employer in a given year.

sources.title: How to File Your Quarterly Tax and Wage Reports

passages.q: Which quarterly reports does ESD expect, and how is this one filed or a filed one changed?
passages.a: Every employer in Washington needs to file 2 tax and wage reports each quarter. Washington employers need to file quarterly: A tax and wage report for unemployment insurance. A combined tax and wage report for paid leave and WA Cares. ... Log into SecureAccess Washington (SAW) to access EAMS and file a quarterly report online. ... Changing a report you filed ... Log into SecureAccess Washington (SAW) to access EAMS and make changes to your quarterly report.

passages.q: Which hours are reported for hourly and for salaried employees?
passages.a: When reporting hours, round up to the next whole number. We don't accept any fractions of hours. Salaried employees: Report the actual hours an employee worked. If you don't track hours, report 40 hours per week for full-time employees. ... Severance pay, bonuses, tips and gratuities: Report zero (0) hours.

sources.title: Penalties for Late or Incomplete Tax Payments and Reports

passages.q: What does ESD charge if the Q3 report is filed or the tax paid after November 2, 2026?
passages.a: If your tax payment is late, we will charge you interest at a rate of 1% of total taxes due per month. We also charge a late payment penalty fee for overdue taxes: First month: 5% of total taxes due or $10, whichever is more. ... We charge a $25 penalty for each late report. ... In some cases, you can ask us to waive penalties for filing a late report or tax payment.

passages.q: Does every employee line carry a SOC code ESD accepts?
passages.a: Provide a SOC code or job title for each employee in your unemployment tax report to avoid a penalty. This requirement started with reports filed for Quarter 1 of 2024. ... The code will be 6 digits. ... Valid SOC codes do not end in a zero. ESD accepts only SOC codes that end in 1 through 9. ... You cannot change SOC codes once you file.

passages.q: What is the 2026 taxable wage base, and how are wages above it treated?
passages.a: You only pay taxes for wages up to the taxable wage base. We consider anything more as excess wages. While you report excess wages, you do not pay taxes on them. Year | Taxable wage base: 2026 | $78,200; 2025 | $72,800 ...

passages.q: How is the employer's 2026 total tax rate made up, and for how long does it apply?
passages.a: We send your tax rate each year in December. It applies to the entire next calendar year. ... Your total tax rate: experience tax rate + social tax rate + EAF. ... The fee ranges from 0.02% to .03%, depending on your rate class.

sources.title: Unemployment Insurance Trust Fund Forecast, June 2026

passages.q: Did the wage base change for 2026, and is a solvency tax added this year?
passages.a: State law increased the taxable wage base from $72,800 to $78,200 in 2026. ... The flat social tax rate is 0.60% for 2026 and will be 0.61% in 2027. ... An employer's social tax rate starts with the flat social tax rate, with a cap of 1.22%. Then we graduate it by rate class. ... For 2028 the solvency tax rate is 0.20%. all other years were 0%.

passages.q: Is Tomas Arvelo's concrete finishing work covered employment that belongs on this report?
passages.a: The term "employment" shall not include services which require registration under chapter 18.27 RCW or licensing under chapter 19.28 RCW rendered by an individual when: (1) The individual has been and will continue to be free from control or direction over the performance of the service, both under the contract of service and in fact; ... (5) ... and has registered for and received a unified business identifier number from the state of Washington; ... and (7) On the effective date of the contract of service, the individual has a valid contractor registration pursuant to chapter 18.27 RCW or an electrical contractor license pursuant to chapter 19.28 RCW.

sources.title: RCW 50.24.014, Financing special unemployment assistance - Financing the employment security department's administrative costs - Accounts - Contributions

passages.q: Why is the EAF 0.02% for this employer and not 0.03%?
passages.a: (1)(a) ... Contributions to this account shall accrue and become payable by each employer, except ... at a basic rate of two one-hundredths of one percent. ... (b) ... Contributions to this account shall accrue and become payable by each employer, except ... those qualified employers assigned rate class 20 or rate class 40, as applicable, under RCW 50.29.025, at a basic rate of one one-hundredth of one percent. ... (2)(a) Contributions under this section ... shall not be deducted, in whole or in part, from the remuneration of individuals in the employ of the employer.

sources.title: WAC 192-310-010, What reports are required from an employer?

passages.q: When is the Q3 2026 tax and wage report due?
passages.a: The quarterly tax and wage reports are due by the last day of the month following the end of the calendar quarter being reported. ... So, reports are due by April 30th, July 31st, October 31st, and January 31st, in that order. If these dates fall on a Saturday, Sunday, or a legal holiday, the reports will be due on the next business day.

passages.q: What must each employee's line on the report show?
passages.a: (a) Tax report. Each calendar quarter, every employer must file a tax report with the commissioner. The report must list the total wages paid to every employee during that quarter. (b) Report of employees' wages. ... This report must list each employee by full name, Social Security number, standard occupational classification code or job title, and total hours worked and wages paid during that quarter. ... These standard occupational categories are identified by a six-digit numerical code.
